newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Talks thin but sentiment firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Talks thin but sentiment firm.

text.p: A lack of inspiring factors kept the high sulphur fuel oil market quiet on Wednesday but prices were well-supported by expected demand from the bunker market, traders said.
The 380-cst grade was offered at $93.5 per tonne, compared with the $92.5 traded level on Monday.
The quiet fuel oil swaps market pushed players to the sidelines but a shortage for the 180-cst grade bunker fuel oil boosted sentiment, traders said.
The April fuel oil swaps were littled changed from Tuesday's levels at $98.75/$99.50. May swaps were heard at $97.75/$98.50 against $97.75/$98.25.
Routine cargoes are still coming in from the Middle East but the number is slightly smaller than usual, traders said.
"The market has been quite slow recently and the only thing to look forward to is the Trade Development Board (weekly residual stocks) data tomorrow," said on trader.
Ample supplies from Indonesia's state-owned oil company Pertamina, standing at over four million barrels in April, kept dampening the already gloomy LSWR market, traders said.
"April supplies are slightly higher than normal but demand is extremely thin, which makes the market really bearish," said one trader.

"I think demand from Japan will pick up only in May when the summer season starts," the trader said, adding that prices should soon test $15.00 per barrel, compared with Tuesday's $15.50 offered level.
Demand emerged from South Korea as the Korean Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) issued a tender to buy two 600,000-barrel cargoes of LSWR for June delivery.
One cargo is for delivery between June 3-7 and the other is for June 26-30, both to the ports of Ulsan or Pusan.
The tender closes April 15 and is valid for one day.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
APR FUEL OIL SWAPS 98.75/99.50 98.75/99.25
MAY FUEL OIL SWAPS 97.75/98.50 97.75/98.25
*Dollars per barrel
--Singapore newsroom (+65-870 3571)
